steps.numerals: Build a triad on each degree of a scale and you have the chords of the key. Roman numerals name them by degree, in capitals when they’re major and small letters when they’re minor: I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi and vii°, which is diminished. In {c} major, V is {gMajor}. In {g} major, V is {dMajor}: the numeral stays and the notes change.
steps.chooseChord: The key’s chord plays, then the chord asked about. Count up from the tonic to its root.
steps.onStaff: Now on the staff, with more chords of the key. The lowest note is the root.
steps.shape: Three chords are major (I, IV and V), three are minor (ii, iii and vi) and one is diminished (vii°). The same pattern holds in every major key, so a chord progression can move to any key with its numerals unchanged.
steps.build: Now play them. The tonic is marked: count up to the root, and stack thirds on it with the notes of the scale.
